title: ZTIE dynamic-run outcome data contract (v1)
description: The derived RUN OUTCOME produced by the Story 2.3 DYNAMIC lane (detonation chamber) for one intake artifact routed to the dynamic_detonation lane, and the ONLY dynamic-lane shape allowed to cross the Forensic -> Hub boundary (RD-013) — the sixth envelope kind on the Hub gate. It records WHAT ran, HOW it was executed host-native via SSM on ONE ephemeral EC2 launched from the Story 2.0 launch template inside the Forensic isolated VPC, the containment facts, and the hard-TTL teardown outcome. It is NOT behavioral telemetry (that is Story 2.4 — this schema has no field for captured behavior) and it is NOT a verdict (no verdict/safe/approved/forward/pass_fail field; execution_status/outcome describe the ORCHESTRATION, never the artifact's safety; the verdict is Hub-side/human-gated, Phase 4). The full command log stays in Forensic (RD-009) behind a pointer; only bounded, byte-capped tails cross. Allow-list: additionalProperties false at every level; every field typed and enum/length/range-bounded. Integrity-keyed by intake_id + sha256. DERIVED-ONLY. CONTAINED + EPHEMERAL: host_native, no_docker, isolated_subnet, no public IP, IMDSv2, a hard TTL (RD-001 / RD-007 / RD-008).

contract_version.description: Dynamic-run-contract schema version. Pinned SEPARATELY on the Hub validator (DYNAMIC_RUN_CONTRACT_VERSION) so this envelope kind versions independently of the other kinds (2.2's lesson). The Hub rejects unknown-version envelopes fail-closed.

intake_id.description: The intake UUIDv4 this run outcome is for. The Hub upserts the outcome onto the tracking record keyed by this.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw artifact body that was detonated. Integrity key, bound to intake_id; the Hub rejects an outcome whose sha256 does not match the tracked record.

detonated_at.description: RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the detonation run completed (the orchestrator finished handling it) in Forensic.

run.description: The derived run outcome: what host ran it, how it was executed, how it was contained, and how it was torn down. EVIDENCE only — never a verdict.

lane.description: The lane this outcome belongs to. Always 'dynamic_detonation' (matches the routing contract's lane enum).

artifact_class.description: The class label the run was based on (from the Story 1.2 classification / 1.3 routing).

outcome.description: How the RUN ended, from the orchestration's point of view (completed / execution_error / launch_error / timed_out / delivery_error). NOT a safety verdict about the artifact — EVIDENCE of the controlled run.

instance_id.description: The ephemeral EC2 instance id that ran the artifact, for audit correlation. Absent on launch_error (no host was created).

launched_from_template.description: True iff the host was launched from the Story 2.0 launch template via ec2:RunInstances (NOT CloudFormation-per-run). A required containment fact — recorded even on launch_error (false then).

launch_template_id.description: The Story 2.0 launch-template id the host was (or would be) launched from (e.g. lt-...). Read from the /ztie/detonation/launch-template-id SSM parameter, never hard-coded.

launch_template_version.description: Optional launch-template version used ($Latest / $Default / a number).

instance_type.description: Optional instance type the host ran as (e.g. t3.small).

started_at.description: Optional RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the detonation run started.

duration_ms.description: Optional wall-clock duration of the orchestrated run in milliseconds.

error_reason.description: Optional short, bounded, non-executable reason when outcome is an *_error / timed_out (e.g. 'RunInstances failed: InsufficientInstanceCapacity'). Never raw content.

containment.description: The blast-radius containment facts for this run, recorded as EVIDENCE that the detonation was properly contained (RD-001 / RD-008). Every field is a fact the orchestrator asserted at launch time, not a verdict.

host_native.description: Always true. Execution is host-native via SSM SendCommand on the ephemeral EC2 (RD-001). The artifact is never run in the Hub.

no_docker.description: Always true. No Docker / container is used on the detonation host (RD-001 — a container would distort behavioral telemetry). The artifact runs directly on the ephemeral host.

isolated_subnet.description: Always true. The host launched into a PRIVATE_ISOLATED subnet of the Forensic detonation VPC (no IGW / NAT / 0.0.0.0/0) — it cannot phone home (RD-008).

public_ip.description: Always false. The host is launched with no public IP association (belt-and-suspenders on top of the isolated subnet).

imdsv2_required.description: Always true. The launch template requires IMDSv2 on the host.

execution.description: How the artifact was executed host-native via SSM, recorded as EVIDENCE. The FULL command log stays in Forensic behind output_s3_bucket/key; only the bounded tails cross. NOT a verdict — ssm_status / exit_code describe how the run ENDED, not whether the artifact is safe.

mechanism.description: How the host-native command was issued. 'ssm_send_command' = the AWS-managed AWS-RunShellScript document via ssm:SendCommand (the Story 2.3 delivery choice, RD-026).

ssm_command_id.description: The SSM command id of the host-native execution, for audit correlation. Absent when the run never reached execution (launch_error / delivery_error).

ssm_status.description: The terminal SSM command invocation status (AWS's own set), or 'not_run' when execution was never reached. EVIDENCE of how the host-native command ended — never a verdict.

exit_code.description: The artifact command's process exit code, when SSM reported one. A RUN fact (0 = ran clean, non-zero = ran and errored) — NOT a safety verdict.

stdout_tail.description: Byte-capped (<= 4096) TAIL of the command stdout for a quick operator glance. Bounded, derived; the FULL log stays in Forensic behind output_s3_key. Inert text, never executed.

stderr_tail.description: Byte-capped (<= 4096) TAIL of the command stderr for a quick operator glance. Bounded, derived; the FULL log stays in Forensic behind output_s3_key. Inert text, never executed.

output_truncated.description: True iff the crossed tails were truncated from a larger full log (which stays in Forensic).

output_s3_bucket.description: Forensic S3 bucket holding the full command output log (RD-009 — the full log stays in Forensic; only the tails + this pointer cross). Absent when no log was captured.

output_s3_key.description: Forensic S3 key of the full command output log (runs/<intake_id>/detonation-output.json).

teardown.description: The hard-TTL / teardown facts for this run (RD-007). The 5-minute hard TTL (`shutdown -h +N` baked into the Story 2.0 launch-template UserData) is the safety backstop: every ephemeral host self-terminates even if the orchestrator dies. This records the configured TTL and whether teardown was actually observed.

hard_ttl_minutes.description: The hard TTL in minutes the launch-template UserData enforces via `shutdown -h +N` (RD-007; 2.0 default 5). A blast-radius / cost bound, not a verdict input.

shutdown_behavior.description: The instance-initiated-shutdown behavior set at RunInstances time. 'terminate' means the scheduled halt tears the host down (the expected value); recorded so a misconfiguration is visible.

teardown_observed.description: True iff the orchestrator observed the host reach a terminated / shutting-down state before it finished. False does NOT mean the host survived — the hard TTL still fires independently; it means the orchestrator did not wait to witness it. An instance confirmed STILL RUNNING past its TTL is a SEV finding and is recorded via `teardown_note`, never silently.

terminated_at.description: Optional RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the host was observed terminated / shutting down, when teardown_observed is true.

teardown_note.description: Optional short, bounded, non-executable note about teardown (e.g. 'observed shutting-down at TTL' or a SEV note if the host outlived its TTL). Never raw content.
